body:
# Independent audit: discounted projective surface repair

Audited source:
`candidate 668d91587751e139`.


scale-free logarithmic budget, the weighted power budgets, and the
normal/parity assembly all check. No scalar deficit is presumed to
vanish for the actual selected-minimum stress.

## 1. The density envelope and exact discount

Let the intrinsic conditional face dimension be `k`, the continuous
body dimension be `d`, and set

```
V=(L_-+L_+)/2,  a=V/L_0.
```

The unequal-radius surface theorem, combined with the common concave
numerator, gives `R_0>=mean(R_-,R_+)`, where
`R_i=(g_i H_i)^(1/(d-k))`. The perspective inequality with middle
denominator `V` therefore gives

```
g_0 H_0/V^d >= N_k(F_-,F_+),
F_0 >= a^d N_k(F_-,F_+).
```

The atom version uses the minimum. No concavity of `L^-d` is asserted;
the loss from concavity of `L` is exactly the factor `a^d<=1`.
Positive-part numerators cause no gap, because both positive weighted
endpoint values belong to the positive concave numerator domain.

## 2. Why the discount controls the actual optimizer measure

The optimizer is taken over the compact fixed-marginal class with
actual support-roof contact, without imposing either `L` contact or
old-law convex order. Its canonical output-roof partition has the
same properties as in the separately audited contact-cell theorem:
each existing restriction is an unrestricted strong-surplus optimizer
for its own restricted endpoint marginals, and its actual outputs
form disjoint Borel pieces.

For each restriction, the strong-surplus inverse maps reconstruct
BOTH endpoints from the midpoint almost everywhere. Consequently the
tuple factor `a` is a single measurable function of that midpoint on
this restriction. The inverse-map area proof gives its density
`h<=N_k(F_-,F_+)`. Thus the density of the discounted pushforward is
exactly `a^d h`, and the preceding envelope proves that it is at
most `F_0`.

This addresses the main possible gap: merely knowing an averaged
bound for several tuples above one midpoint would not justify using
one chosen `a` there. Here endpoint reconstruction proves the required
determinism for the analyzed optimizer restriction. Disjoint actual
output labels then allow the discounted bounds to be summed, including
positive-mass ties, without any roof-cell factor.

## 3. The capacity class is linear and closed

On the compact endpoint product, `L>0` makes `a^d` continuous and
bounded. Therefore

```
b_#(a^d pi)<=omega
```

is a family of linear weakly closed inequalities against nonnegative
continuous output functions. The resulting coupling class is convex
and compact. Every smooth strongly convex surplus optimizer belongs
to it by Section 2.

The usual approximation, nonnegative finite separation, and compact
finite-intersection argument therefore produce one coupling in this
class above the prescribed old midpoint law in convex order. It is
not necessary to introduce a nonlinear excess-budget class. The
endpoint tuple labels remain available in the exact positive error
measure

```
E_pi=b_#[(1-a^d)pi].
```

The equalities and inequalities

```
rho=D_pi+E_pi,
D_pi<=omega,
(rho-omega)_+<=E_pi
```

hold as measures, not merely as total-mass estimates. The lower bound
`a>=ell/U` also gives `rho<=(U/ell)^d omega`, so absolute continuity
survives the final compactness argument automatically.

## 4. The logarithmic payment is the correct rearrangement invariant

Arithmetic-geometric mean gives

```
-log a <= log L_0 - mean(log L_-,log L_+) = delta_log.
```

Hence `1-a^d<=1-exp(-d delta_log)`. The integrated right-hand gap is
`integral log L d rho` minus a fixed endpoint constant. The explicit
tangent continuation of `-log` and the maximum over the affine
`A_i` give a finite global convex test agreeing with `-log L` on
the body. Convex-order improvement therefore makes this integrated
gap no larger than the old one. Jensen for the concave function
`1-exp(-d s)` proves the exact bound

```
E_pi(total)<=m[1-exp(-d Delta_old/m)].
```

The source correctly distinguishes this fixed-endpoint gap from
`log(L_0/V)`, whose integral is not determined by the midpoint law
and fixed endpoint marginals. It does not compare old and new
expectations of the latter tuple function.

## 5. Weighted power budgets

For `0<p<=1`, the negative of `L^p` has the same finite convex
extension construction, so `c_p<=T_p<=T_p,old`. Under the probability
measure `L_0^p dpi/T_p`, one has

```
E[a^p] = integral V^p dpi/T_p >= c_p/T_p.
```

Convexity of `s^(d/p)` gives

```
integral L^p dE_pi
 <= T_p[1-(c_p/T_p)^(d/p)].
```

The function `T-c_p^(d/p) T^(1-d/p)` is increasing on `T>=c_p`,
which justifies replacing `T_p` by `T_p,old`; the last linear bound
follows from Bernoulli's inequality. This includes `p=1,d=1` without
a limiting convention. Zero mass is handled separately. The direct
log proof avoids needing an interchange in the `p`-to-zero limit.

## 6. Assembly and marks

The final constraints consist of Borel conditional marginals, the
actual support graph, the continuous tuple discount, domination by
the fixed weighted target kernel, and countably many convex-order
tests. They are stated in original physical coordinates, so no
measurable face frame, roof enumeration, or density representative
is required. The existing selector applies.

Summing the at most `2^n` parity classes gives a baseline
`2^n omega` and the SUM of their actual error measures. There is no
extra factor multiplying the error. The perspective
`m[1-exp(-d Delta/m)]` is concave and homogeneous, so classwise
and normalwise integration gives the stated global logarithmic bound.

Marked-source reconstruction preserves the source mark and its
conditional midpoint mean. It need not preserve individual endpoint
marginals conditional on that mark. Accordingly the entropy comparison
is correctly asserted only within the normal/parity classes where
those endpoint marginals are fixed.

The theorem supplies an exact quantified replacement for missing
zero Jensen contact. It does not show that the actual old physical
surface deficit is small enough to establish the OC constant.

## 7. Added exact sharpness example

The added Section 9 correctly realizes equality in the nonlinear
one-parity tradeoff. On identical cube facets at bases `-1,+1`, the
identity pairing of continuous coordinates uniquely maximizes the
continuous quadratic midpoint moment. The midpoint base is fixed,
so this is also the relevant physical quadratic optimization after
discarding that constant coordinate. Any midpoint law above this
old law in convex order is therefore the same law.

For `L(z)=1+b-b|z|`, every tuple has constant discount
`a=(1+b)^(-1)` and constant logarithmic gap `log(1+b)`.
The actual middle capacity is exactly `a^d` times the old uniform
facet law. Therefore the positive excess, the exact error measure,
and the nonlinear logarithmic bound coincide. The weighted `L^p`
nonlinear bounds also coincide. The source correctly limits this
sharpness assertion to one parity class.

A minor notation clarification was requested and patched: in the quadratic
identity, `X,Y` must explicitly denote continuous endpoint
coordinates. Full physical endpoint coordinates have distinct bases
and cannot literally satisfy `X=Y`. The intended calculation is
valid with this clarification, now present in the source.

## 8. Added affine-weighted relative entropy

Section 10 also passes. For positive affine `q`, the perspective

```
F_q=q log(q/L)
```

has a finite global convex extension on the compact body by taking
the maximum over affine `A_i` of the supremum, over a bounded
parameter interval, of `q t-A_i exp(t-1)`. Every restricted affine
expression is at most `F_q` on the body, and an active `A_i=L`
together with `t=1+log(q/L)` attains equality. Positivity outside
the body is not needed.

Using `q_0=mean(q_-,q_+)`, the direct expansion is

```
delta_q/q_0
 = log(L_0/V)
   + sum_i [q_i/(2q_0)]
       log{[q_i/(2q_0)]/[L_i/(2V)]}.
```

Thus it is exactly `-log a+KL(p||s)`. Nonnegativity of the latter
term gives the claimed pointwise discount payment. Affineness makes
the total `q` mass a fixed endpoint quantity, and full convex order
makes the integrated `F_q` Jensen gap no larger than the old gap.
Weighted Jensen therefore proves all displayed nonlinear and linear
error bounds for the SAME already selected coupling.

Replacing `q` by `q+epsilon` correctly handles nonnegative affine
weights: `q log q` is continuous at zero, `log L` is bounded, and
the relevant functions converge uniformly. The zero-total-`q` case
has zero weighted error and zero endpoint gap. The source correctly
forbids replacing `q` by an arbitrary hinge: both the affine
midpoint identity and the fixed total weight would be lost.
